title: gate add keeps an option's do text as written, or refuses prose, instead of storing it split into words
goal: backlog.py gate add with a --do that is prose (not a command) either stores the text as written or refuses it naming the form it wants, so ST-kp5oq4sr's g1 do map is not a list of single words and an apostrophe does not fail with No closing quotation

run:
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os, json, glob
tool = os.path.abspath("_tools/backlog.py")
def run(root, *a):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, tool, "--root", root, *a], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr
def trial(prose):
    root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    iid = run(root, "new", "story", "--title", "T", "--goal", "g", "--touch", "src/a.py")[1].split()[2]
    code, out = run(root, "gate", "add", iid, "--id", "g1", "--question", "How to word the note", "--option", "a",
                    "--option", "b", "--recommendation", "a", "--do", "a=" + prose, "--do", "b=ST-00000000")
    stored = None
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "_backlog", iid + ".json")):
        gates = json.load(open(f)).get("gates") or []
        stored = gates[0].get("do", dict()).get("a") if gates else None
    if code == 0:
        return stored == prose, out
    return "No closing quotation" not in out and ("command" in out or "item id" in out or "prose" in out) \
        and "--do" in out and "not a command line" not in out, out
good = True
for prose in ("Reword the line in the doc", "Reword the doc's line"):
    ok, out = trial(prose)
    good = good and ok
sys.exit(0 if good else 1)
